defects.description: Components of a rule whose condition was added with WhenAsync/UnlessAsync are described with IsConditional false, because only rule.HasCondition and not rule.HasAsyncCondition is passed to DescribeComponent.
MapLength only writes maxLength when the maximum is greater than zero, so MaximumLength(0) or Length(0, 0) produces no maxLength at all.

MapRange reads the bounds by casting context.Validator to IBetweenValidator instead of from the validator metadata, so the schema mapper depends on concrete validator interfaces, ignores GetMetadata overrides and throws InvalidCastException for a custom validator that reports an InclusiveBetween/ExclusiveBetween kind.
IsInEnum on a flags enum is silently dropped from the schema without the diagnostic that the request requires for every rule that cannot be expressed.
PrecisionScale bounds are written as inclusive maximum/minimum (±10^(precision-scale)), although that value itself has one integer digit too many and fails the validator; they must be exclusive.

ToJson serializes with JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping, so titles, descriptions and error messages containing <, > or & are written unescaped, which allows script injection when the schema is embedded in an HTML page.

Every object schema gets additionalProperties: false when IncludeUnvalidatedProperties is false, which nobody asked for and makes the schema reject payloads containing the model's other (unvalidated) properties.
Precision_scale_sets_bounds_and_multiple_of only checks the type and multipleOf, not the minimum/maximum bounds its name says it tests.
Describes_dependent_rules only asserts that DependentRules is not null, which is always true, instead of checking the described dependent rule.
Resolve adds a property for a rule on a member marked [JsonIgnore] (and can mark it required), although such a member is never serialized; [JsonIgnore] is only honoured for unvalidated properties.

defects.description: TryCreate forces an execution trace (and thus a diagnostics scope on every validation) whenever a debugger is attached, which nobody requested and which breaks the pay-for-play rule while debugging.
ValidatorStartingEvent.Instance is populated whenever the call captures a trace, even with CaptureInstances off, so the (possibly sensitive) validated instance is handed to every global listener.
The duration histogram, declared with unit "s", records Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds, so durations are reported 1000 times too large.
Validators() pushes child validators onto the stack in forward order, so sibling child validators are enumerated in reverse start order instead of depth-first start order.
The JSON writer writes Exception.ToString() as the exception message, exposing full stack traces and inner exception details in logged traces.
On .NET 6+ the JSON writer escapes strings with System.Text.Json, contrary to the requirement that the writer has no JSON library dependency and behaves the same on every target framework.
The text formatter appends a "(slow)" marker to rules taking at least a new SlowRuleThreshold (100 ms by default), a feature that was not requested.

Only the synchronous Filter branch (this line) reports filtered elements; the AsyncFilter branch a few lines below skips the element without calling recorder?.ElementFiltered(), so elements filtered with WhereAsync are not counted.

Json_writer_escapes_strings_and_reports_exceptions only asserts the rule outcome, not that the property path with quotes, backslash and control characters round-trips through the JSON, so escaping is not checked.

defects.description: Problem_details_registration_does_not_change_global_defaults never resolves the formatter, so the registration's configure delegate (which runs lazily on first resolution) is never invoked and the assertion on the global title cannot fail.
Builder_does_not_change_options_it_was_given creates the builder without passing the options object it then asserts on, so the assertions that the given options stay unchanged are trivially true.
CreateProblemDetailsSerializerOptions turns on WriteIndented, so problem details responses are pretty-printed, which the requested web defaults with null values left out do not include.

The problem details converter matches member names on read with a case-sensitive switch, so a document with "Title" or "Errors" (for example from Newtonsoft.Json defaults) puts those members into Extensions instead of the standard members, although member matching on read must be case-insensitive.
The problem details converter writes the type member unconditionally, so a problem details object whose Type is null is written with "type": null instead of leaving the null standard member out.

The serializer-neutral ValidationProblemDetails model is bound to the System.Text.Json converter with a [JsonConverter] attribute, coupling the core model to one serializer and bypassing the opt-in registration through AddFluentValidationConverters.
WithStatus rejects 599 because the upper bound check uses >= 599, although its message and documentation accept HTTP status codes from 100 to 599.

CreateDetail includes the attempted value whenever custom state is enabled, so opting into custom state alone exposes attempted values (possibly passwords or personal data) that must stay out unless IncludeAttemptedValue is set.
DistinctMessages compares messages ignoring case, so messages for the same property that differ only in letter case are dropped as duplicates although only identical messages should be merged.
The existing ValidationResult.ToDictionary() now groups property names case-insensitively, merging keys such as "Name" and "name", which changes existing behaviour that had to stay unchanged.

defects.description: The syntax table of docs/rulesets.md has no row for quoted names ('two words', "two words", with a doubled quote as escape), so the quoting syntax the request asks to document is not documented.
Expression_selects_rules_in_async_validation validates with IncludeRuleSets("Create") instead of IncludeRuleSetsMatching, so the async path of rule set expressions is not exercised by the test.

Expression_selects_the_same_rules_as_rule_set_names computes byExpression with IncludeRuleSets(ruleSets) instead of IncludeRuleSetsMatching(expression), so it compares IncludeRuleSets with itself and never checks the expression.

RuleSetNameExpression.ComputeHashCode uses the case-sensitive Name.GetHashCode() while equality compares names case-insensitively, so equal expressions such as "create" and "Create" get different hash codes.
ParseUnary does not count '!'/'not' towards the nesting depth, so a chain of more than 64 negations is not rejected and deep input can overflow the stack.
The tokenizer accepts '~' as a negation operator (and treats '~' as an operator character, so it can no longer appear in an unquoted rule set name), which the requested syntax does not include.

CharEquals compares with the culture-sensitive char.ToUpper, so glob pattern matching depends on the current culture (e.g. 'i' and 'I' do not match under tr-TR) and is inconsistent with the ordinal case-insensitive comparison of names.
IncludeRuleSetsMatching(string) treats an empty or whitespace expression as "*" and runs every rule instead of rejecting it as a syntax error.
RuleSetExpression.Parse adds every distinct expression text to the static cache without any size bound, so expressions taken from user input can grow memory without limit.

ChildValidatorAdaptor.GetSelector creates RuleSetExpressionValidatorSelector directly instead of through ValidatorOptions.Global.ValidatorSelectors.RuleSetExpressionValidatorSelectorFactory, so a custom selector factory is ignored for child validators.

defects.description: hsl_css_color() does not pass its luminosity argument to generate_hsl(), so the luminosity the task requires every new method to honour is ignored.
hwb_css_color() converts HSV to HWB inline in the provider instead of using RandomColor.hsv_to_hwb / the hwb format of RandomColor, where the task places the conversions.

color_pair() picks a dark foreground only when the background's relative luminance exceeds 0.5 instead of about 0.18 (where black and white give equal contrast), so mid-luminance backgrounds get a light foreground with poor contrast and many more tries are needed.

_HEX_PATTERN (with the matching len(digits) in (3, 4) expansion in _parse_hex at line 57) also accepts 4- and 8-digit hex colors with an alpha channel, which the task does not ask for (it asks for #rrggbb input) and whose alpha is then silently dropped.

_NUMBER uses the nested quantifier ((?:\d+)+...), so parse_color() / contrast_ratio() on a long digit run that fails to match (for example 'rgb(' + '1' * 30 + '!') backtracks exponentially (regular-expression denial of service).
tones() divides by (size - 1) instead of (size - 2) when interpolating the size - 1 derived tones, so the last tone of a monochromatic palette never reaches the dark shade and the spread is uneven.
The hwb_css_color stub is missing from faker/proxy.pyi after the hsl_css_color stub, so the stub file is not the regenerated one the task requires and type checkers do not know Faker.hwb_css_color.
test_alpha_is_ignored_by_opaque_formats passes alpha=0.5 to both generate() calls it compares, so it does not check that an alpha is ignored by the hex format.
test_contrast_ratio_draws_no_random_value re-seeds the generator after calling contrast_ratio(), so any random value drawn by contrast_ratio() is reset and the test cannot detect it.

defects.description: _check_level strips and lower-cases the level before validating it, so levels such as "Bachelor" or " master " are accepted instead of raising ValueError for a value that is not one of the six level literals.

The age computed from the birthdate in education() compares (month, day) with <=, so a person is counted one year younger on their birthday itself and levels completed at exactly that age are rejected.
The es_ES grade draws the Matrícula de Honor chance from the module-level random module instead of self.generator.random, so the output does not follow the generator's seed.
The fr_FR education provider subclasses the en_US locale provider instead of the base education Provider, making one locale depend on another locale's data and overrides.
_mark_out_of draws the ordinary mark with triangular(lowest, highest, mode), so a mark can round to the full mark outside the full_mark_share draw instead of being capped at highest - 1.
profile() only generates the education fields when "education" is named, so profile(fields=["highest_degree"]) returns no highest_degree field.
The regenerated faker/proxy.pyi has no stub for academic_title(), so the education provider's academic_title method is missing from the Faker type stubs.
test_mention_matches_mark only checks that the mention is one of the known mentions and the mark is in range, not that the mention corresponds to the mark.
test_default_profile_random_sequence_is_unchanged does not request the education field in the second profile, so it does not check that asking for education leaves the other fields unchanged.
test_localized_education_record parses the CLI output with eval() instead of ast.literal_eval(), executing whatever the command printed.

defects.description: blood_group() picks from tuple(self.blood_group_frequencies), i.e. only the keys, so every blood group is equally likely and the result is not weighted by the locale's population frequencies as the task requires.
practitioner_name() strips and upper-cases sex before checking it, so values such as "m", "f" or " x " are accepted instead of raising ValueError for anything other than "M", "F", "X" or None.

The first de_DE female practitioner name format hard-codes the title "Dr. med." instead of using {{prefix_medical_female}}, although doctor titles belong to the person provider; female full names therefore never get the person provider's other titles (Prof. Dr. med., Dipl.-Med.).

_CRM_PATTERN matches the number with the nested quantifier ((?:\d+)+) (the 4-6 digit length is only checked afterwards in is_valid_crm), so is_valid_crm() on a long digit run that fails to match, such as 'CRM/SP ' + '1' * 30 + '!', backtracks exponentially (regular-expression denial of service) in a validator documented for checking user data.

nhs_check_digit() returns "0" when the modulus 11 check value is 10 and "" when it is 11, the wrong way round: numbers whose check value is 10 (which are invalid) are accepted by is_valid_nhs_number() with check digit 0, and valid numbers whose check value is 11 (check digit 0) are rejected and never generated.

is_valid_colegiado_number() accepts province prefixes 1 <= p < 52, so prefix 52 (Melilla) is rejected although its docstring and the es_ES province codes cover 01-52, and colegiado numbers generated for Melilla fail validation.

profile() draws blood_group from the class attribute of the base medical Provider imported directly into the profile provider (from ..medical import Provider) instead of calling self.generator.blood_group(), so it bypasses the generator's locale provider and always uses the base (US) frequencies instead of the locale's table.

faker/proxy.pyi has no stub for prefix_medical_female() between the prefix_medical and prefix_medical_male stubs, so the stub file is not the regenerated one the task requires and type checkers do not know Faker.prefix_medical_female.

TestVitalSigns.test_abnormal asserts `abnormal is not None` for each sample, which is always true for a list, so it does not check that every vital_signs(abnormal=True) result has at least one value outside its normal range.

TestMedicalLocales.test_blood_group asserts counts.most_common(1)[0][1] >= counts[most_common], which holds for any counts, so it does not check that the table's most frequent blood group is the most generated one; only the > 250 bound checks anything.

test_default_output_is_unchanged calls the second profile() with only the default fields, never naming a medical field, so it does not check that requesting the opt-in medical fields leaves the default fields unchanged.

changes.testsAtSeededHead: Ran 2026-11-21 at seeded head 28f4b9bb: 5 failed, 3474 passed, 10 skipped, 1 deselected (failures: TestBusinessDays::test_add_business_days_zero, TestBusinessDays::test_weekend_date_between_ignores_holidays, TestHolidayProvider::test_holiday_dates_between, test_holiday_dates_between_end_is_exclusive, test_holiday_dates_between_several_years).

defects.description: _holiday_dates() calls the private HolidayCalendar._compute() instead of calendar.dates(), bypassing the per (locale, year) cache of the rule engine, so every business-day check recomputes three years of holiday rules.

_is_business_day() is decorated with functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None) on an instance method, so every (provider, day) pair ever queried stays in an unbounded process-wide cache that also keeps every provider (and its generator) alive; dates taken from caller input grow memory without limit.

The enumeration fallback of _random_day_matching() builds candidates with range(span), which leaves out the end day although the range is inclusive, so when the random draws miss and the only matching day is the end day, business_date_between() / weekend_date_between() raise ValueError instead of returning it.

add_business_days() with n=0 moves a day that is not a business day forward to the next business day (and its docstring documents this), instead of returning the day unchanged; the request defines only adding n business days.

is_holiday() returns True for every Sunday, not only for public holidays and substitute days of the locale's calendar, which the request does not ask for and which disagrees with holidays() and with the business-day weekend configuration (e.g. he_IL, where Sunday is a working day).
holiday_dates_between() iterates range(first.year, last.year) without including last.year, so holidays in the year of the end date are never returned (a range within a single year returns nothing).
Victoria Day is defined as the Monday on or before 25 May, so in years where 25 May is a Monday (e.g. 2015, 2020, 2026) it falls on 25 May instead of the Monday preceding 25 May (18 May).

建国記念の日 (National Foundation Day, 11 February) is not wrapped in _holiday()/Observed, so when it falls on a Sunday (e.g. 2018, 2024) no 振替休日 substitute holiday is generated, although the request requires ja_JP substitute holidays.

test_is_business_day_observed_holiday asserts that Saturday 4 July 2026 and Saturday 1 January 2022 are not business days, which holds for any weekend day, so it does not check the observed (substitute) days 3 July 2026 and 31 December 2021 that its comments describe.
test_holiday_with_year only checks that holiday(year=2019) returns a non-empty name and a date in 2019, not that the pair is one of the holidays of 2019 for the locale.

changes.testsAtSeededHead: Ran 2026-11-21 at seeded head b7e10d3a with `npx jest --coverage=false`: 18 suites (6 failed, 12 passed), 835 tests: 827 passed, 8 failed (groupErrorsByPath › should keep a property named __proto__ as an ordinary key; flattenValidationErrors › should escape ~ and / in JSON Pointer paths, › should render map keys in brackets and as pointer segments, › should include the constraint context only when asked to; conditional validation › should only format the errors of properties whose condition holds; nested validation › should be formatted with the keys of nested sets and maps; formatErrorTree › should accept a custom indentation string or width; error path helpers › escapeJsonPointerToken › should escape ~ before /). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.prod.cjs.json` and `npx prettier --check --end-of-line auto` on src/formatters and test/formatters pass.

defects.description: escapeJsonPointerToken replaces '/' with '~1' before replacing '~' with '~0', so the '~' of the produced '~1' is escaped again and a key containing '/' becomes '~01' instead of '~1', violating RFC 6901 (every pointer path with a '/' in a key is wrong).

flattenValidationErrors never adds the constraint context to an entry: options.includeContext (documented on FlattenValidationErrorsOptions and passed on by toProblemDetails) is ignored, although the task requires includeContext to add the context of the failed constraint.

describeValue quotes string values by escaping only double quotes, so newlines, carriage returns and control characters (including ANSI escape sequences) of a user-supplied value are written raw into the formatErrorTree output with showValues, allowing forged log lines and terminal escape injection when the tree is logged.

resolveIndent rejects an indent width of 0 with a RangeError (the check is indent <= 0), although its message and the option's contract accept any non-negative integer, so formatErrorTree(errors, { indent: 0 }) throws instead of rendering an unindented tree.

formatErrorTree builds the property label with its own bracket/property rule instead of the shared appendDotSegment of error-path.util, duplicating the path-rendering logic that the task requires to live in one place shared by the formatters and ValidationError.toString().

groupErrorsByPath creates each group by plain assignment, so an error path of __proto__ (a property name that can come from validated input, for example a nested object or map key) replaces the prototype of the returned object with an array instead of becoming an own key: the messages for that path vanish from the enumerable result and the object inherits array members (prototype poisoning of the result).

groupErrorsByPath drops a message that is already listed for the same path, a de-duplication nobody asked for: the task specifies each path mapped to its messages in the order the constraints were reported, so the result does not have one message per failed constraint.

hasRecordedValue treats a recorded value of undefined as not recorded (it tests error.value !== undefined instead of whether the error has a value property), so a property that failed because it was undefined gets no value in flattenValidationErrors/toProblemDetails with includeValue and none in formatErrorTree with showValues.
'should not modify the given errors' takes the JSON snapshot after calling flattenValidationErrors, so it compares the errors with themselves and cannot detect a mutation by the formatter.

'should pass includeValue and includeContext to the entries' only checks the paths and the first message of problem.errors, never the value or context members, so it does not check that toProblemDetails passes includeValue and includeContext on.

changes.testsAtSeededHead: Ran 2026-11-21 at seeded head ad64f5a3 with `npx jest --coverage=false`: 7 suites failed, 17 passed (24); 11 tests failed, 901 passed (912 total); failing: @JsonSchema decorator › should reject keywords that are not plain JSON; IsDateString › should agree with the exported JSON Schema; IsISO8601 › should agree with the exported JSON Schema; JSON Schema export of array checks › should keep the tightest size when ArrayNotEmpty and ArrayMinSize are combined; JSON Schema export of custom decorators › should report partial conversions and constraints a converter declines; JSON Schema export of number checks › should keep the tightest of several bounds; JSON Schema export of string checks › identifiers and formats › should map IsEmail, IsUrl and IsIP to formats, which are reported as partial conversions; ... › should report the strict ISO 8601 option as a partial conversion; ... › lengths › should keep the tightest bounds when length decorators are combined; ... › patterns › should map character class checks to the validator.js patterns; JSON Schema export of type checks › should treat maxDecimalPlaces as a number without an exact equivalent. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.prod.cjs.json`, eslint and prettier (--end-of-line auto) on the touched files: clean.

defects.description: getDefinitionName checks whether a validation schema is registered by reading the private validationMetadatas map of MetadataStorage through an `any` cast instead of calling MetadataStorage.hasValidationSchema(), although the task requires the exporter's metadata access to go through MetadataStorage methods.

buildPropertySchema only records a constraint as not expressed when no conversion is returned; a partial conversion (exact: false, e.g. IsEmail, IsUrl, IsIP, strict IsISO8601, IsNumber with maxDecimalPlaces, or a custom converter returning partial keywords) is emitted without being listed under x-class-validator with unknownConstraints: 'annotate', so the looser schema is not reported.

The IsDivisibleBy converter emits multipleOf with the divisor as given, so a negative divisor (e.g. IsDivisibleBy(-4)) produces multipleOf: -4, which is not a valid JSON Schema (multipleOf must be strictly greater than 0); the sign does not affect validator.js's check and must be dropped.

The Length converter only writes maxLength when the maximum is truthy, so Length(0, 0) (or Length(min, 0)) produces no maxLength and the schema accepts strings of any length that validator.js rejects.

The IsAlphanumeric converter emits the pattern ^([0-9A-Za-z]+)+$ with a nested quantifier, so a JSON Schema validator using a backtracking regex engine (such as ajv on Node.js) takes exponential time on a long alphanumeric string followed by a non-matching character (regular-expression denial of service on untrusted payloads); ^[0-9A-Za-z]+$ accepts the same strings.

mergeSchemas keeps the smaller of two lower bounds (minLength, minimum, exclusiveMinimum, minItems) with Math.min instead of the larger, so combining e.g. Min(1) and Min(10), or ArrayNotEmpty and ArrayMinSize(3), gives a schema looser than validate().

toPlainJson silently converts valid Date instances to ISO 8601 strings instead of rejecting them as non-JSON values, so @JsonSchema keywords and converter results containing dates are accepted and rewritten, which nobody asked for and contradicts the documented rejection of class instances.
'should map IsDivisibleBy to multipleOf' only checks the type of the property declared with IsDivisibleBy(-4), not its multipleOf, so the mapping of a negative divisor is not tested.

'should not share objects between two exports' asserts that the second export's minLength is >= 0, which holds whether it is 3 or the 0 written into the first export, so shared objects between exports are not detected.

changes.testsAtSeededHead: Ran 2026-11-21 at seeded head 55943e2f with `npx jest --coverage=false`: 23 suites (5 failed, 18 passed), 2205 tests: 2199 passed, 6 failed (canonicalizeLocale › rejects "de-toolongsubtag"; custom constraints and message catalogues › passes the messages of ValidateBy on; locale › each › should use the prefix of the messages option; MessageResolver › messages option › can override only the prefix of the catalogue messages; registered locales › lets later registrations override earlier entries; whitelist validation with a locale › should let the messages option override the forbidden property error). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.prod.cjs.json` and `npm run lint:check`: no errors.

defects.description: @ValidatorConstraint registers its messages option only when an explicit name is also given, so a constraint class named after its class (no name option) silently loses its catalogue entries although custom constraints must be able to provide them under their constraint name.

ValidateByOptions declares a messages option, but ValidateBy (lines 30-37) never passes options.messages on to registerDecorator, so the per-locale messages given to ValidateBy are never registered in the catalogues.

LOCALE_TAG_PATTERN makes the hyphen optional inside a repeated group ((-?[a-z0-9]{1,8})*), so a long alphanumeric value that fails to match (e.g. 'de' followed by many digits and '!') backtracks exponentially (regular-expression denial of service, reachable from an Accept-Language header as in sample11); it also accepts tags such as 'de-toolongsubtag' that are not valid BCP 47 tags.

registerLocale spreads the existing catalogue after the given one, so entries already in a catalogue (including every bundled entry) win over newly registered ones: a later registration cannot override an existing message, contrary to its documented merge behaviour.

The Polish isLength 'tooLong' message chooses the plural form of 'znak' from the minimum (constraint 1) instead of the maximum it states ($constraint2), so e.g. Length(1, 5) gives 'co najwyżej 5 znak' instead of '5 znaków'.

findEachPrefix takes the $each prefix of the catalogue that provided the message before the $each given in the call's messages option, so a prefix overridden for one call is ignored whenever the catalogue has its own, although the documented rule is that the messages option wins.

The forbidNonWhitelisted message is built in the executor from getLocaleCatalog/en via whitelistMessageTemplate() (lines 452-456) instead of through the MessageResolver, although message creation in the executor must go through one resolution function; as a result it ignores the call's messages option and the locale fallback chain (de-AT gets English).

insertEachPrefix also treats '{each}' as a placeholder for the each prefix, a second token syntax nobody asked for (catalogues use the $each token) that also removes a literal '{each}' from any message.

'are passed to the message builder only when no catalogue has an entry' only checks the resulting message, never that the constraint's defaultMessage was not called, which is what its name says it tests.
'copies the registered catalogue' mutates isInt on the passed object but asserts on isEmail, so it cannot detect that the registry keeps a reference to the passed catalogue instead of a copy.

changes.testsAtSeededHead: Ran 2026-11-21 at seeded head afeed6b6 with `npx jest --coverage=false`: 4 of 27 suites failed, 7 failed, 1908 passed (1915 tests); failing: rules builder › invalid rules › should throw when length() has a minimum greater than its maximum, rules builder › invalid rules › should throw when isByteLength() has a minimum greater than its maximum, schema conversion › rulesToValidationSchema › should convert built-in rules with their arguments and options, schema conversion › rulesFromValidationSchema › should throw for unknown validation types, schema conversion › rulesFromValidationSchema › should report rules with invalid constraints and modifiers that cannot apply to each element, validation options of builder-configured classes › groups › should use the always validator option as default, validation schemas › should throw when a built-in validation type has invalid constraints. `npm run lint:check` and `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.prod.cjs.json` pass.

defects.description: The validator of an inline rule created with validateBy() catches any exception thrown by the user's validator function and reports the value as invalid, which nobody asked for: decorators created with @ValidateBy let such exceptions propagate, so programming errors in an inline check are silently turned into validation failures.

isSize() requires a size greater than zero, so arrayMinSize(0) and arrayMaxSize(0) throw a RuleDefinitionError ("must be a non-negative number") although @ArrayMinSize(0) and @ArrayMaxSize(0) are valid decorators and the builder must accept the same parameters.

resolveOptions() copies the always rule option only when it is truthy, so a rule configured with { always: false } gets no always option and falls back to the validator's global always option, unlike the same decorator with always: false (the rule is then checked although it opted out).

isPositive() re-implements the isPositive check and its default message inline with ValidateBy instead of using the existing IsPositive decorator / isPositive function, contrary to the requirement that the field builder reuses the existing validator functions and default messages rather than duplicating them.

assertRange() checks only that min and max are non-negative numbers and never compares them, so length(min, max) and isByteLength(min, max) with min > max are accepted instead of throwing when the rule is built, as the task requires.

applySchemaRule() falls back to calling any field builder method whose name equals the schema validation type (with all the schema's constraints as arguments) when the type is not a built-in rule name, so a schema taken from a configuration file or other untrusted input can invoke arbitrary builder methods (custom, validateBy, the constructor...) instead of being rejected as an unknown validation type.

ruleToSchemaRule() never writes the rule's context into the schema validation, so rulesToValidationSchema() loses the context option although ValidationSchema supports it and the conversion must keep message, groups, always, context and each.

'should never change the builder a new builder is derived from' asserts on the derived builders (extended and derived) only and never on base, so it cannot detect that deriving a builder changes the builder it was derived from.

'should strip unknown properties of nested plain objects when whitelisting' checks that the top-level config has no password property, but the unknown password was added to config.database, so the assertion is always true and the stripping of the nested object is not checked.
